title: I started building a news app as a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered.
body:
It felt like every news platform was designed to keep me scrolling through noise rather than helping me understand the world. I wanted something different. I wanted a way to filter out the clutter and get straight to the facts that affect my daily life.

Building Headlinne meant rethinking how we consume information. We focused on using AI not to generate content, but to organize it. The goal was simple. Create a tool that acts like a personal editor, learning what you care about and delivering only the relevant updates.

It has been a long process of trial and error. We had to figure out how to balance automation with human-like curation. The result is a platform that respects your time and your intelligence. We are moving away from the endless feed model and toward something more intentional.

Technology should serve our curiosity, not exploit our attention spans. That is the core philosophy behind everything we build.
cta: You can see how we are changing the way people read the news at HEADLINNE.com.
